Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist | Data Engineering & Analytics

Edinburgh, UK | tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 | linkedin.com/in/tmh-example

PROFILE
Data scientist with 6 years’ experience in analytics and data science, including 4+ years as a data scientist. Experienced in building analytical workflows with Python, SQL, BigQuery and dbt, and translating business needs into reliable data products. Developed scheduled forecasting and batch-scoring workflows, and contributed to a Dockerised experiment-planning application hosted on Cloud Run. Strong statistical foundation and keen to develop further in data engineering and platform work.

KEY SKILLS
Python: pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, Streamlit, pytest
SQL: BigQuery, batch scoring, query-based analytics
Data workflows: dbt, scheduled notebook jobs, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench
Engineering tools: Git, Docker, Jupyter
Analytics: data modelling, A/B testing, causal inference, time-series forecasting, Bayesian statistics
Visualisation and reporting: Looker, R Markdown

EXPERIENCE

Data Scientist | Thistlebox (meal-kit subscriptions), Edinburgh
Feb 2022–Present
- Build and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests per year for growth and product teams; created a sequential testing calculator used by around 25 colleagues.
- Developed a weekly, six-week-ahead demand forecasting workflow by recipe and region using LightGBM and calendar, price and menu-position features. The scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook writes forecasts to BigQuery for operations reporting in Looker.
- Improved forecast WAPE from 23% to 14%; the work was associated with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.
- Developed an XGBoost churn propensity model, scored weekly in BigQuery, to target retention offers to top-decile customers. A 10% holdout validation found churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group.
- Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
- Since 2025, written pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage.
- Built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential experiments and wrote its Dockerfile; the data platform team handles deployment to Cloud Run.
- Present results to leadership monthly and have delivered internal “Stats for PMs” training three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail, Glasgow
Sep 2020–Jan 2022
- Performed customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

SELECTED PROJECT
Image Classification | Personal learning project, 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep learning course, achieving approximately 80% accuracy.
- Tools: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

EDUCATION
MSc Statistics, University of the Lothians | 2020 | Distinction
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand

BSc Mathematics, University of the Lothians | 2019

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Swahili (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured and professional CV with strong quantified evidence: approximately 40 experiments per year, 23% to 14% WAPE improvement, estimated 9% food-waste reduction, 60% test coverage and measurable adoption of the sequential-testing application. The chronology, education and technical stack are easy to understand. The main content limitation is that the document presents a strong data-science and analytics profile rather than the ownership of a senior data platform. The profile is appropriately cautious about further developing in data engineering, which is truthful but makes the seniority mismatch visible.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly section headings, conventional reverse chronology, readable bullets and standard text-based formatting. Relevant terms such as Python, SQL, BigQuery, dbt, Docker, Cloud Run, Vertex AI Workbench, Git, data modelling and batch scoring are present. AI screening probability is moderate: the document should be discoverable for BigQuery, dbt, Google Cloud and Python-related searches, but it does not demonstrate several high-weight senior data-engineering terms from the advert, including production data-platform ownership, cloud-warehouse operation at scale, query optimisation, dimensional modelling, governance, access policies, CI/CD, Airflow and GKE. These should not be added unless supported by the candidate's experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the Google Cloud environment at an implementation level: the candidate uses BigQuery daily, schedules work in Vertex AI Workbench, contributes a Dockerised application hosted on Cloud Run, and maintains dbt models. It also demonstrates collaboration with product, growth, operations, leadership and the data platform team, supporting Halden Pay's Together and Ownership values. Professional English is shown through native-English language status, leadership presentations and internal training. However, the candidate's material does not establish ownership of a production data platform or cloud warehouse at scale, advanced SQL query optimisation on large datasets, strong dimensional modelling, platform governance or access policies, or evaluation of open-source architecture tools. The material also does not show graph modelling or Portuguese. These are genuine role-fit gaps rather than CV defects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the phrase "Experienced in building analytical workflows with Python, SQL, BigQuery and dbt, and translating business needs into reliable data products" with the more precise "Experienced in building production analytics workflows with Python, SQL, BigQuery and dbt, and translating business needs into reliable data products." This keeps the strong platform-relevant positioning while avoiding any implication that the candidate owns a central data platform.

2. In the Key Skills section, reorganise the skills into ATS-searchable categories and make the Google Cloud experience explicit: use categories such as "Programming: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, Streamlit, pytest"; "Data warehouse and transformation: SQL, BigQuery, dbt, analytics-layer data modelling, batch scoring"; "Google Cloud: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Cloud Run"; and "Engineering: Git, Docker, Jupyter." This should replace the current mixed categories without adding unsupported tools such as Airflow, GKE, CI/CD or MLflow.

3. In the Thistlebox experience section, change the bullet "Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer" to "Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer, supporting recurring forecasting, churn-scoring and reporting workflows." This connects the existing warehouse and transformation work more directly to production workflow operation while remaining supported by the CV.

4. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise "Built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential experiments and wrote its Dockerfile; the data platform team handles deployment to Cloud Run" to "Built and containerised a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential experiments by writing its Dockerfile; the data platform team deploys it to Cloud Run." This improves keyword visibility for containers and Cloud Run while preserving the important boundary around deployment ownership.

5. In the Profile or Key Skills section, change "data modelling" to "analytics-layer data modelling with dbt". The current wording can be read as a claim of broad or dimensional modelling expertise, which is not established in the candidate information; the revised wording accurately reflects the documented experience.

requirements.requirement: Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Strong data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud
requirements.quote: "scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook writes forecasts to BigQuery" and "data platform team handles deployment to Cloud Run"

requirements.requirement: Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
